newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to consolidate Iraqi debt.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to consolidate Iraqi debt.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim cabinet said on Monday it would urgently begin work on calculating the total debt Iraq owes to the cash-strapped Balkan country, government officials said.
"The cabinet empowered Trade Minister Daniela Bobeva to co-ordinate talks on consolidation of amounts owed by Iraq," a government spokeswoman told reporters.

The debt, estimated between $1.2 billion and $2 billion, was accumulated between 1982 and 1990, when Bulgaria, like other countries in Eastern Europe, supplied Baghdad with arms and other goods in return for crude oil during the Iran-Iraq war.
Bobeva said Iraq and other countries in the Middle East and Latin America owed Bulgaria some $3 billion.
Some transactions were made between companies, and the trade ministry is now expected to consolidate their claims.
Bulgaria currently relies entirely on foreign loans to repay $1 billion in debt payments due this year.
Bobeva said repayments could be negotiated in the form of barter deals, including grain.
An unidentified third country had shown interest in acquiring the Iraqi debt in return for grain supplies, local media reported recently.
Bulgaria needs to import grain urgently as its current supplies will last less than 20 days. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
